meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-inspired; partnership law codified under Luxembourg Civil Code and Commercial Companies Act 1915, with hybrid modern partnership elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Treaty (1996, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML Law), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended by Law of 25 July 2020 implementing the 5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (LSC), as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 establishing the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp); Law of 27 December 2011 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Register of Commerce and Companies; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulations on the RBE; FATF Recommendations incorporated by CSSF Circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity card copy of each natural-person UBO and each natural-person general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state authority / passport or national ID office in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued in an Apostille Convention state; otherwise consular legalization by the competent Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate in the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and current good-standing extract of any corporate general partner or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar or commercial registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified French or German translation by a Luxembourg sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) for the Luxembourg statutory representative and professional domiciliation agreement for the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notaire) or licensed domiciliation agent, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg notarial deed (domestic notarization; no foreign apostille required for the local deed)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner declaration (formulaire RBE) and know-your-customer profile for every legal and natural person holding or controlling 25% or more of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance officer of the Luxembourg law firm / fiduciary subject to Luxembourg AML Law Article 3
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal KYC verification under the AML Law; no certifying authority outside the Luxembourg financial sector

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at inception and every 12 months of all UBOs, partners, directors, general partners and signatories against: (i) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions and CAP lists; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for USD-denominated wire transfers; (iv) UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions; (v) Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) CNI list and CSSF public warnings; (vi) FATF non-cooperative jurisdictions and grey-list notifications. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are treated in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and the EU AML Directive, including family members and close associates. All screening results are documented, retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship and made available to the CSSF or FIU upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online application portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin alphabet characters. Non-Latin names must be transliterated into French or German official spelling and submitted together with a translation of the meaning. The legal-form indication 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must be in French. The name must be visually and phonetically distinguishable from all existing RCS entries; English-only names are permitted if written in Latin characters and not contrary to public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal or provisional objection by the RCS/LBR, the applicant or the mandated notary must file a reasoned administrative appeal with the registration commission of the Tribunal d'arrondissement (Luxembourg District Court) within one month of the refusal notice. The appeal must annex the original name-search receipt, the reserved name, the refusal grounds and any proposed corrective amendment. No extension of a valid name reservation is available; a fresh reservation may be filed immediately after the court determines that the name may be used, or after the applicant submits an amended name to the RCS.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a SCSp only if the registered office is a physically verifiable address in Luxembourg operated by a licensed domiciliation agent or by the company itself. A pure mailbox without any personnel, books or management activity will not support a claim of Luxembourg tax residence or treaty benefits. For an AdTech/SSP platform engaged in programmatic advertising, the Luxembourg substance office may outsource technical processing to EU/EEA data centres, but must retain corporate housekeeping, board decisions, accounting and KYC files in Luxembourg. A virtual office is therefore accepted at initial registration, subject to a substance compliance plan to be audited within the first fiscal year.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the RCS registration office, CSSF or Luxembourg direct-tax/VAT inspector for a low-risk standard AdTech platform; the probability rises to 40–50% where tax treaty relief, advance pricing agreements or VAT refund applications are made without demonstrable Luxembourg-owned assets and payroll.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name availability and reservation certificate (certificat de disponibilité de nom)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff for an RCS name-reservation request; non-refundable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign identity and corporate documents (per document set)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (Luxembourg) or originating foreign competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fixed administrative fee, plus Luxembourg consular legalization scale where applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French or German translation of constitutional documents, IDs and registry extracts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted at the Luxembourg District Court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark rate for certified translation (per page / flat quote)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial act of formation of the SCSp (if notarial form elected) or certification of private partnership deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff set by the Ministerial Tariff Decree for notaires, subject to minimum and maximum scale

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed RCS registration fee pursuant to the Law on Luxembourg Business Registers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / LBR electronic publication system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee under the Law of 27 December 2011 as amended

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) for each beneficial owner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed LBR/RBE online filing fee per legal entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional domiciliation and registered-office provision (12-month advance, initial deposit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation agent (agréé en domiciliation) or CSSF-supervised corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for licensed domiciliation; no statutory cap but CSSF circular requires arm's-length pricing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel and AML compliance onboarding retainer (KYC, PEP/sanctions screening, due diligence dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market billing rate (EUR 250–450 per hour) under a fixed engagement letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative appeal contingency reserve (name clearance or RCS registration dispute)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-standard contingency reserve; refunded if not used

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013, Articles 101-1 to 101-8 (Section 5bis: Société en Commandite Spéciale); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de commerce et des sociétés - RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the e-RCS electronic filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (contrat de société) executed by private writing or notarial deed, deposited electronically with the RCS together with the manager's declaration and specimen signature
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the SCSp is a fiscally transparent limited partnership whose capital is freely fixed in the Partnership Agreement; contributions may be cash, in-kind, or in industry; no escrow account or capital deposit certificate is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription schedule for partnership interests in the SCSp as set out in the Partnership Agreement is hereby approved and ratified in full; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorized to notify the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Manager Name] is appointed as sole manager (gérant) of the SCSp, with power to open bank accounts, execute contracts, retain advisers, and file statutory returns; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the manager shall take all actions required to file the Partnership Agreement with the RCS, effectuate RESA publication, obtain VAT registration, and commence the programmatic advertising exchange business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online RCS search portal and e-RCS filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a preliminary availability search on the RCS electronic database. Luxembourg does not operate a formal name-reservation system; exclusivity is obtained at the moment of RCS registration. Proceed immediately to filing once a distinctive name is confirmed. The SCSp name must contain the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp'.
required_dossiers: Identity of the general partner proposing the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the name as identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registration, select a modified name and re-file; no fine is incurred for a pre-registration name refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / Luxembourg notary (notarization mandatory only if real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) including corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, object clause limited to programmatic AdTech activities, partnership capital and contribution schedule, rights and powers of the general partner, and profit attribution. The agreement must be signed by at least one general partner and one limited partner. If contributions consist only of cash or movable assets, private writing is sufficient.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extracts for the general partner/manager
Contribution schedules and asset valuations, if in-kind
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS requires a notarial deed (e.g. real-property contribution), re-execute before a Luxembourg notary and re-deposit; cure filings within the month are not subject to an additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorized by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the drafted Partnership Agreement, partners' identification, and UBO declarations to the bank. The bank performs know-your-customer due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering. No capital-deposit certificate is required by law for the SCSp; the account may be funded with the agreed contributions after RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Passports and proof of address of partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information under KYC rules, supply a cleared source-of-funds memorandum; disproportionate refusal may be escalated to the CSSF mediation desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - e-RCS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Partnership Agreement, the manager's declaration with specimen signature, the registered-office consent, and the RCS registration form E1 via the e-RCS portal. Pay the filing fee online. The RCS validates legal-form conformity, checks the name, and issues the RCS registration number and extract.
required_dossiers: Executed Partnership Agreement (scanned or EDI-compliant XML)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a demande de complément (completeness query), respond within one month via e-RCS with the missing documents; an RCS refusal is appealable to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the RCS automatically publishes the registration excerpt in the electronic compendium (RESA). The publication includes the SCSp's name, form, registered office, object, managers, and legal entity number. No separate publication fee is payable beyond the RCS filing fee; monitor RESA for the attestation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication contains errors, file a corrective excerpt via e-RCS; if publication is refused, verify compliance conditions and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the UBO declaration on the LBR portal identifying all natural persons who ultimately control or own the SCSp (general partner and any ultimate beneficial owners), with percentage of interest. This is mandatory under the Law of 13 January 2019.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of each beneficial owner (passport or national ID card)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing triggers an administrative fine; the remedy is an immediate supplementary filing with an explanatory note; penalties may be contested before the Luxembourg administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number via MyGuichet.lu using the standard VAT application (formulaire n° 1 TVA) and the identification form (formulaire n° 2022). Programmatic advertising and SSP services follow the EU B2B place-of-supply rule (reverse charge); Luxembourg VAT applies only if the customer is a non-business taxpayer established in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: VAT questionnaire with activity description and revenue projections
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT certificate is delayed, the AED issues an acknowledgement and the business may issue invoices referencing a pending VAT number; delays beyond two months may be escalated to the AED tax director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional Establishment Authorization and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for SMEs (Direction générale des classes moyennes); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp hires local staff or occupies commercial premises in Luxembourg, the manager must obtain an autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011, applied for on MyGuichet.lu. Employer registration with the CCSS and accident insurance (AAA) is mandatory within 8 days of first hiring. For a pure remote digital AdTech operation with no local employees or physical presence, these requirements are not triggered.
required_dossiers: Manager's identity and criminal record extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusal of the establishment authorization is appealable hierarchically to the Ministry of the Economy, then to the Administrative Court; late social-security registration is cured by a retroactive declaration with a penalty-reduction request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises; Administration de l'environnement (environmental permitting authority)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No AdTech-specific statutory operating license; the only potentially applicable permit is the 'autorisation d'établissement' (business establishment authorization), required solely if a physical commercial establishment with local staff is operated in Luxembourg

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - EIA not required; the digital office-based activity falls below Annex I/II thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 May 1999 on Environmental Impact Assessment; no environmental operating permit is triggered for pure server/office activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC discharges; office HVAC and server cooling must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 31 August 2010 on indoor climate and energy performance; compliance with the Law of 9 April 2012 on WEEE and the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management; stationary fuel-burning equipment, if any, must meet EU eco-design and emissions thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification for the registered office from the Administration des services de secours (Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Service); structural load review for technical/server-room floors; Labour Inspection (Inspection du travail et des mines - ITM) workplace clearance under the Labour Code (Book III) covering ventilation, lighting, electrical installations, first aid, and mandatory staff representation if the headcount reaches or exceeds 15 employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified electronic portal MyGuichet.lu (Guichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Prepare and notarize the SCSp limited partnership agreement and register the SCSp at the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu. 2. Obtain the RCS registration number (numéro d'immatriculation). 3. File VAT registration application with the AEDT, providing proof of RCS registration, registered office address in Luxembourg, details of the general partner (including any foreign corporate general partner), and description of actual services; appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (représentant responsable) where required for non-established taxable persons. 4. Use the RCS number and VAT number for national filings; the SCSp, being fiscally transparent, normally receives no separate direct-tax TIN, but direct tax filings are made by the partners at their respective tax offices, with the SCSp's Luxembourg identification referenced in information returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a US-style check-the-box election. An SCSp is, by default and as a rule, fiscally transparent: it is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax; profits and losses flow through to partners according to the partnership agreement and are taxable or creditable in the partners' own jurisdictions. There is no statutory election to convert the SCSp into a CIT taxpayer as such, although participants may structure the chain through Luxembourg corporate entities to achieve different cross-border results. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD, Luxembourg Law of 21 December 2018) must be observed because foreign characterization of the SCSp may otherwise trigger disallowances; no grandfathering applies to new structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) – EU Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established taxable persons: registration required for the first taxable supply in Luxembourg (no de minimis threshold). Luxembourg-established small enterprises may be exempt below EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) under Article 57 LTV. For a programmatic ad exchange platform, B2B supplies to other Luxembourg taxable persons are reverse-charged and B2B supplies to non-Luxembourg taxable persons do not create Luxembourg VAT registration; Luxembourg VAT registration becomes mandatory if the platform makes B2C supplies in Luxembourg or supplies goods or local services subject to Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) system for B2B VAT. E-invoicing is lawful if authenticity, integrity and legibility are guaranteed. B2G e-invoices must be submitted in the European standard EN 16931/PEPPOL format for contracts awarded by central public bodies (national public procurement portal). There is no digital stamping or mandatory pre-clearance API; the AEDT may, on audit, require electronic extraction of invoicing data under applicable VAT inspection powers. Standard VAT invoices must state the SCSp's RCS number, VAT number, service description, place-of-supply rule, rate, and, for reverse-charge intra-community supplies, the customer's VAT number and the words 'autofacturation'/'auto-liquidation' where relevant.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies where physical goods are exported outside the EU/neighbouring territories, provided departure is evidenced within the legal timeframe by a VAT-validated customs export declaration (DAE) and transport documents, and the exporter is identified for VAT in Luxembourg. Services: the platform's programmatic advertising, DSP/SSP, and technical service fees are not 'exported goods'; they fall outside Luxembourg VAT under B2B place-of-supply rules when supplied to a taxable customer in another State, or under B2C rules when effectively used outside the EU. To substantiate outside-Luxembourg treatment, retain: the service contract; IP address/geolocation or evidence of the customer's place of establishment, actual use, and consumption; the customer's valid VAT registration number for EU B2B supplies; and bank settlement records. Refund mechanism: input VAT on Luxembourg costs (e.g. hosting, local office, marketing) is deductible in the Luxembourg VAT return against Luxembourg output VAT; if no such output VAT arises, a non-established operator may recover Luxembourg input VAT through the 13th Council Directive refund procedure (Form 13 VAT 655) within nine months after the calendar year of the charge, subject to AEDT verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE) validated by Luxembourg Customs and issued through the EU customs ECS/ICS system
Transport documentation demonstrating physical departure: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR if goods movement is present
Commercial invoice, contract or platform settlement statement evidencing the recipient and cross-border commercial terms, together with bank payment/inward remittance proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no general Luxembourg exchange-control repatriation deadline for digital services; the 180-day field is the requested template default and is not itself a Luxembourg VAT due date. Mischaracterisation of place of supply, failure to prove export, or non-compliant zero-rating exposes the SCSp to AEDT reassessment of Luxembourg VAT at 17%, default interest (the LTV/General Tax Law applies late payment interest), administrative fines for infringement of invoicing and declaration rules, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent VAT evasion. The assessment/recovery window is normally five years and is extended in cases of intentional evasion or anti-fraud investigations; any input VAT previously deducted for corresponding costs is clawed back if the underlying output supply is retroactively reclassified as taxable in Luxembourg.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CTF supervision of credit institutions and payment service providers; the BCL implements European Central Bank (ECB) monetary policy and operates TARGET2-LU settlement infrastructure. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign exchange administration authority; FX policy falls under Eurosystem competence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. Both current account and capital account transactions are unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the Codewall, with no exchange control authorization, no surrender requirement, and no differentiated treatment between resident and non-resident SCSp partners. Profit remittances, distributions, dividends, and partnership capital withdrawals may be executed freely via banking channels, provided only that standard payment reason codes and AML/KYC reporting obligations are met. The sole practical hurdles are bank-level compliance documentation and anti-money laundering checks, not statutory convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, minimum surrender ratio, or forced conversion obligation for export proceeds. Receivables from programmatic advertising services rendered to non-EU counterparties may be retained in invoiced currency (typically USD) in any bank account, held in FX, or converted to EUR at the corporate partner's discretion. Final reporting follows balance-of-payments statistics filings (BOP) submitted by resident banks to the BCL, not as a control measure but as statistical observation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / FX Hedging Collateral Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Luxembourg-compliant and EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as those authorized under the CSSF or other EEA regulators may be used for cross-border payments and virtual IBANs; however, they are not full credit institutions and cannot provide lending, foreign exchange forwards, or custody. Offshore (non-EU) EMIs impose material legal constraints under PSD2, the EU E-Money Directive (2009/110/EC), and Luxembourg anti-money laundering law, including the need for a local branch or agent where passporting is not available, client money safeguarding, and full access to partner identity documentation. The SCSp's partnership opacity increases onboarding friction; EMIs generally require a Luxembourg RCS extract, certified partnership agreement, and a breakdown of each partner's economic and voting rights. For a programmatic AdTech platform with significant USD flows, the use of an EU-licensed EMI is viable for collections and payouts, but a tier-1 bank is recommended for the principal operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for directors or partners to appear physically in Luxembourg. Remote onboarding is permitted under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as interpreted by CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 and successive guidance, using eIDAS-qualified electronic identification, qualified video identification, or video-verification combined with certified copies of identity documents. In practice, many tier-1 Luxembourg banks condition onboarding of an SCSp with non-resident general partners and multi-tier limited partners on an in-person or secure remote interview with at least one authorized signatory and the AML compliance officer. Where the general partner is a corporate vehicle, banks will also require KYC on the ultimate natural-person directors of the GP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque partnership ownership chain with silent limited partners and no clear UBO percentage breakdown
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement; up-to-date RCS Luxembourg extract; an org chart showing each partner's direct and indirect percentage of capital and voting rights; authorization letter identifying the SCSp's general partner and its directors; passports and certified proof-of-address for all natural-person UBOs; confirmation that no single partner can be undisclosed under CSSF beneficial-ownership reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AdTech revenue model showing rapid throughput from programmatic bidders, inventory sellers, and demand-side platforms with diverse counterparty geographies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and audited or accountant-reviewed latest financial statements; signed commercial contracts with leading DSPs/SSPs; transaction flow diagrams revealing fee recognition, net settlement mechanics, and match rates; platform licensing/source-code and IP ownership documentation; proof of operational substance including office lease, staff payroll, and IT infrastructure; a written AML risk assessment classifying programmatic ad exchange traffic as low-risk with documented counterparty onboarding procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to/from high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned countries through SSP relationships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated geo-IP and legal jurisdiction blocklist logs; real-time sanction screening and adverse-media screening outputs; anti-money laundering policy with embedded sanctions and PEP filtering; meticulous IP-to-geolocation mapping and suppression screenshots; contractual assurances from supply-chain partners that no served ads originate in or are delivered to sanctioned territories; demonstrable alignment with Luxembourg sanctions regulations and EU restrictive measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore payment gateways or virtual IBANs causing unclear payment origin and layered settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete bank-statement trail connecting virtual IBAN settlements to master account sweeps in the partner's name; executed agreements with payment service providers identifying the SCSp as the merchant/beneficiary; transaction reconciliation reports with matching endpoints for each gateway; confirmation that the gateway is licensed in an EEA state and has passed CSSF/EBA passporting checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions arriving from multiple non-resident partners without clear economic substance or source-of-funds evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds documentation including bank statements, capital contribution bank transfer references, and partner net-worth statements where requested; board resolutions or partner resolutions approving capital calls; subscription documents with payment timestamps; tax-transparent partnership status letter or tax advisor confirmation to explain lack of corporate income-tax burden; audited opening balance sheet if required by the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners shall be routed through SWIFT MT103 or EU ISO 20022 pain.001/004 messages to the SCSp's EUR capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire instruction shall include the partnership legal name, the partnership RCS number, and reference code 'SCSP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' followed by the capital call number. No exchange-control declaration is required; however, the receiving bank will require a copy of the capital call notice, bank reference from the remitting partner's account, and confirmation of the funding currency. For dollar-denominated contributions, the bank may route through a corresponding USD account in New York or via TARGET2 for EUR conversion; the SCSp shall instruct settlement after checking intermediary charges. Fixed-income income or working capital flows from programmatic operations must use Service revenues purpose codes (e.g., 'charges for services' in balance-of-payments classification) and should not be mislabeled as capital contributions to avoid AML misclassification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for non-EU participating banks, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) for EU publishers and vendors, and ISO 20022 pain.001 for batch payouts through corporate banking portals. Settlement to large-scale programmatic counterparties may follow contractual netting; for triggered SSP disbursements, the SCSp should use a dedicated payout sub-account with bank-provided APIs supporting straight-through processing. For inventory acquisition and revenue share payments to non-EU countries, Commercial Letters of Credit may be required where contractual terms demand documentary security; otherwise MT103 wire transfers are used. TARGET2, through BCL, provides real-time gross settlement for EUR flows only, while USD flows will settle via correspondent banking networks (CHIPS or Fedwire) through the bank's USD clearing agent (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas or JP Morgan). The treasury policy shall also consider day-light overdraft controls, value-date optimization, and use of MT101 sweeping to maintain minimum liquidity at the operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (up to 3-6 month tenors) with authorized Luxembourg credit institutions under ISDA or bank-standard netting master agreements, permitted without prior BCL approval.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for settlements in restricted or low-liquidity currencies if the SCSp's SSP activity generates noneurrency cash flows in currencies not fully deliverable; NDFs must be transacted with the banking counterparty's offshore desk and structured to settle in EUR.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and currency swaps) for obtaining USD liquidity while keeping EUR capital at the Luxembourg account, subject to valuation of collateral as acceptable under the bank's treasury policy.

Plain-vanilla European-style FX options (calls and puts on USD/EUR) for risk-capped hedging, provided the option premium is paid out of operational cash-flow and hedging documentation aligns with the SCSp's treasury mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax return of the SCSp and partner income allocation reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline is 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; electronic filing through the eTVA portal; extensions are possible only upon justified request before the original deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty may reach 10% of the assessed tax due, plus default interest at 0.6% per month on outstanding amounts; persistent non-filing allows ACD to issue an official estimated assessment and may trigger enforcement against the general partner's assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and financial statements deposit with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RCS/RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved within six months after financial year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a calendar-year entity the latest standard window is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure after formal notice may lead to a court-ordered filing injunction; repeated non-filing entails civil liability of the general partner or manager and can ultimately result in administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial owner confirmation and transfer update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial RBE declaration is due within one month of RCS registration; any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be declared within one month; a year-end reconciliation of the RBE extract is required as part of the annual register audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate declarations carry administrative fines and criminal penalties under Luxembourg AML law; persistent concealment can lead to court-ordered RBE correction and blocking of distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and recapitulative statement, if VAT registration applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year VAT reporting, the annual VAT return is due by 31 March of the following year; taxpayers on periodic filing must continue monthly or quarterly returns as scheduled.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge up to 10% of the VAT due, statutory interest at 0.6% per month, and, in case of sustained non-compliance, enforced recovery and criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and minute book reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; available for inspection by ACD, RCS, and RBE control authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No filing obligation; must be completed and physically maintained at the Luxembourg registered office no later than the financial statements approval deadline, normally within six months of financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inaccurate registers invalidate corporate procedural evidence and expose the general partner to civil damages; in RCS strike-off proceedings, deficient registers are treated as serious delinquency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp is subject to mandatory statutory audit if it has legal personality and exceeds at least two of the Luxembourg small-undertaking criteria: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees; audit is also compulsory if required by the partnership agreement, a lender, a partner request, or a financial sector regulatory licence. An SCSp without legal personality and below these thresholds is generally exempt from statutory audit, but may voluntarily obtain an audited certificate for investor or regulatory purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the legal accounting framework of 19 December 2002; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for individual and consolidated financial statements. The fiscally transparent SCSp reconciles commercial partnership accounts to partner-level income allocations for Luxembourg income tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain a contemporaneous partner transfer record. Any share transfer or subscription that changes beneficial ownership must be recorded in the statutory register and filed with the RBE within one month of the event. There is no separate annual UBO return, but the annual corporate secretarial review must reconcile the partner ledger, the transfer record, and the RBE extract at every financial year-end; a newly served RBE reconciliation notice must be answered within one month. Failure to update after a transfer is a continuing RCS/RBE delinquency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partner/Managers and Capital Contributions
Minute Book of Partnership and Management Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,250 - USD 4,500 per year for registered agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial support services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 22,000 for a small-to-mid-cap SCSp audit under Luxembourg GAAP; no statutory audit fee is required if the entity is below thresholds and no contractual audit obligation exists

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City: CIT 17% + municipal business tax 6.75% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT = 1.19%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent: no corporate income tax at entity level; profits are taxed in the hands of partners. Corporate general partner (S.à r.l./S.A.) taxed at 24.94%. Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% holding or ≥EUR 6,000,000 acquisition cost, held ≥12 months). IP box: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income (effective rate ≈5.00%). R&D tax credit (Art. 57quater LIR) up to 20% of qualifying research expenditures. Net wealth tax 0.5% on net taxable assets applies to commercial partnerships and the corporate GP.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory cap since 2017; carryback disallowed; losses pass through to partners under fiscal transparency)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 560/5601 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed by the corporate general partner; electronic submission via MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-file portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance tax payments due 15 February, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY ended 31/12/2025 due 31/12/2026); extensions available on justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: name, registered office, RCS number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident GP files for its Luxembourg PE; enter Luxembourg PE registration and foreign TIN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates of the 12-month taxable year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align PE period with head-office accounting year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per annual statutory accounts before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only report PE-attributable profit; attach PE financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: ATAD interest limitation, excessive inter-company royalties, fines, non-business entertainment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Demonstrate arm's length pricing of all cross-border ad-tech service flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of exempt income: participation-exempt dividends and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: only exempt items attributable to Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allocation of SCSp result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident GP: include PE-share of SCSp commercial profit.
Non-resident: only losses incurred by Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable taxable base after loss and exemption relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute in EUR; attach exchange-rate computation for foreign currencies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 17% plus solidarity surcharge of 7%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No entry if PE covered by treaty residence allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax at communal rate (6.75% Luxembourg City).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE located in multiple communes: apportion by payroll and fixed assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments, withholding credits, balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax credit documentation for treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge up to 12% of assessed tax (10% if filed after reminder); monthly late-payment interest 0.8%; administrative fine up to EUR 1,000; deliberate concealment triggers criminal sanctions under Art. 426 AO.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp Fiscal Transparency Return (Partnership Profit Allocation Statement) submitted via MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-file; additional declaration accompanying the GP's Form 560.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; aligned with the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; same deadline as the GP's corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full list of general and limited partners: name, address, tax identification number, jurisdiction of tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partner must provide foreign tax ID and TRC if treaty protection is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit/loss allocation per partner in EUR and percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm allocation follows the SCSp partnership agreement and does not create unintended Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership declaration of each partner and any indirect controlling entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident UBOs: provide passport copies and registered-agent certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Activity description: programmatic advertising exchange, DSP/SSP platform, employees, office, turnover, operational substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must state whether they carry on any activity in Luxembourg beyond passive investment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border related-party transactions: media-buying commissions, data licensing royalties, platform service fees, interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach TP policy, transfer pricing documentation and arm's length benchmarks.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing of transparency statement: fine up to EUR 2,500 and ex officio assessment; allocation may be disregarded and profits re-allocated to the GP; late payment interest 0.8%/month and surcharge up to 12%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends distributed by a Luxembourg capital company; 0% for profit distributions by the SCSp to partners because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and distributions are treated as profit shares, not dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief on Luxembourg-source dividends, the beneficial owner must submit a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its residence state, a beneficial ownership declaration and, where applicable, Form 21 to the Luxembourg ACD. Relief is applied either at source (prior nil-withholding authorization) or by refund claim within 5 years. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a 0% rate applies where the parent holds ≥10% for ≥12 months. SCSp profit distribution to non-resident partners generally requires no Luxembourg WHT; the partner's residence state taxes the allocation subject to the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties is 0% in Luxembourg. No domestic WHT is levied on cross-border interest or IP royalty payments; treaty rates are therefore moot. However, excessive or non-arm's length interest/royalty paid to related parties may be re-characterized as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT under ATAD/GAAR anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and CbC Report triggered at EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue (EU Directive 2016/881). Luxembourg Local File expected where annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 and taxpayer turnover exceeds EUR 3,100,000 (ACD TP circular LIR n° 164/2). Ad-tech inter-company flows must always be documented despite any de minimis threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone ESR statute comparable to UAE. Substance requirements derive from OECD BEPS Actions 5 and 6, the ATAD GAAR, and ACD administrative practice. The SCSp must maintain a Luxembourg-resident general partner with real local presence (office, staff, decision-making for the ad-exchange platform), board minutes, local bank accounts, and commercial contracts. A letter-box SCSp with no operational substance risks re-characterization, denial of treaty benefits and loss of the participation exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating programmatic ad revenue; issuing fictitious media-buying invoices to shift profit to low-tax entities; misallocating SCSp taxable profit among partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Art. 426 AO and Art. 396 Criminal Code: fine up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years; administrative evasion surcharge up to 10% of evaded tax; late-payment interest 0.8% per month; confiscation of illegal gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/gérants of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax and civil damages where fraud was authorized or knewly concealed; criminal conviction triggers travel bans, passport seizure and disqualification from board office for up to 10 years; civil restitution under Art. 1382 Civil Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 560 or the SCSp transparency return; failure to remit quarterly advance payments; refusal to provide TP documentation upon ACD request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge up to 12% of assessed tax; late-payment interest 0.8% per month; administrative fine up to EUR 1,000 per missing return; ex officio assessment with additional penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid withheld taxes and assessed tax where non-payment results from gross negligence; tax authorities may sue the directors personally for the corporate debt; management ban on recidivism; travel bans and asset attachment for tax debts above EUR 5,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Arrangement / Lack of Economic Substance (Shell Company)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the DSP/SSP platform through a substance-less SCSp with no employees, no local office, and central management abroad solely to escape Luxembourg CIT or misuse treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ATAD GAAR (Art. 8bis LIR) disregards the artificial arrangement; reassessment of income with 10% surcharge; denial of participation exemption, IP box and treaty benefits; criminal fraud prosecution if supported by false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable under Art. 710-1 of the Law on Commercial Companies for unlawful distributions and artificial structures; personal civil liability for the hidden tax debt if the GP is liquidated; travel bans and asset freezes in cross-border tax fraud investigations; extradition risk in serious international cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ad-tech exchange without KYC/AML controls; using the SCSp to move fraudulent ad-click or money-mule proceeds; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Luxembourg FIU; concealing UBO disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended): money laundering offence — imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to EUR 1,250,000 for individuals; legal entities fined up to EUR 5,000,000; CSSF administrative fine up to EUR 1,000,000; asset freezing and confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner face personal criminal conviction for AML conspiracy; civil liability to defrauded advertisers and partners; travel bans and freezing orders; automatic disqualification from professional management; extradition risk in organized cross-border fraud networks.
